exposure: BMI category (morbidly obese vs. super obese)
cohort: 494 parturients with a BMI exceeding 40 kg/m2 at delivery, including 469 morbidly obese and 25 super obese individuals
finding: Among women receiving regional anesthesia, super-obese parturients had greater intraoperative bleeding, a higher proportion of hypotensive episodes, and a greater vasopressor requirement than morbidly obese parturients.
mod_finding: This study examined cesarean delivery in morbidly obese and super obese parturients, finding that super-obese parturients had greater intraoperative bleeding, a higher proportion of hypotensive episodes, and a greater vasopressor requirement than the morbidly obese parturients.
